questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that the courses suggested were adapted to my study program and in line with what I already have had at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Of course, it helped that I have a connexion to France and know people there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any kind of assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing off campus was a challenge. It took a lot of effort and paperwork to get things settled. I recommend arriving earlier than I did to have more time finding a room. I arrived one week prior to my study start.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is great and the locations, you can choose, are better (in my opinion) than the ones for on campus-housing. Although, as mentioned before, it is a challenge to find housing in Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is very simple. It happened through an online plateform and the mobility coordinator is very good at helping, answering emails and give your the necessary advice. At arrival, I had to fill out a "certificate of arrival paper". That's it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Any help needed was provided by the staff present on the first day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My program included only compulsory courses (no elective courses), so the registration was automatic.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No comments here.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my opinion, the level of the courses is approximately the same as at my home university. However, I had a total of 10 courses at the same time, whereas at KU, I used to have 2 at the same time. More structure and organisation was needed from my side to adapt to this new rhythm.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was part of an extensive project, so we had a lot of group work. Compared to UCPH, we had less practical work (laboratory, in my case). Another important aspect to mention is that, in France, you typically have small exams every week and not one big exam at the end of the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Entreprise et Entreprenariat (English, Economics and Entrepreneurship), Gestion de projet industriel (Industrial project, Computer science), Qualité environnementale (Sustainability and food storage), Formulation (Nutrition, enzymes and formulation)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Gestion de projet industriel (Industrial project) was my favourite course. 
Note : If you choose the same exchange program as me, you will get those courses and cannot choose others.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is less expensive in France compared to Denmark. Housing was very expensive. Museums are free for all under 26 in Paris. Personal expenses such as hairdresser and so, are less expensive in France as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Weekly sport classes, after-class parties, ski trips, Erasmus parties, tourism and sightseeing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The tourism and sightseeing together with other Erasmus students are a great way to discover the city and get to know other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city. It has a lot to offer and a lot of small hidden gems.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, as I am half French. If you don't know the French culture at all, I recommend meeting up with French people to get the full experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to parties and events as much as you can, especially at the beginning of the exchange, registrer in a gym or any other sport, try to talk in French as many times as you can.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: French people are straightforward.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the history of the city of Paris.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Plan your exchange. Start finding housing early. Make a budget. Be prepared that you might face some challenges and things don't always go as planned, but you always find a solution.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me, it was the academic outcome. I learned more than I expected to do and it really enriched my ability to work on my own and with others.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was finding an apartment.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
